content.value_statement: Agents that use RDF context need traceable reasons for beliefs, goals, and committed plans. This skill structures context as BDI mental states with ontology patterns and validation queries.
actual_capabilities: Maps RDF world states into beliefs, desires, intentions, plans, and justifications.
Explains how to ground mental states in world-state references.
Adds temporal validity and provenance patterns for explainable agent reasoning.
Provides SPARQL competency questions for validating BDI models.
Shows integration patterns for SEMAS, JADE, JADEX, and logic augmented generation.
limitations: Provides modeling guidance, not a runnable ontology validator.
Assumes users understand RDF, Turtle, and SPARQL basics.
Requires adaptation before use in production agent frameworks.
Does not replace privacy, safety, or domain review of agent actions.

use_cases.title: Design Explainable Agent Reasoning
use_cases.description: Model why an agent formed beliefs, selected goals, and committed to plans.

use_cases.title: Validate Semantic Agent Models
use_cases.description: Use competency questions to check provenance, motivation, and temporal validity.

use_cases.title: Bridge RDF and BDI Systems
use_cases.description: Translate external RDF context into mental states for multi-agent workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Mental States
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner mapping from context to BDI concepts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BDI mental states skill. Identify the world states, beliefs, desires, and intentions in this scenario: [scenario].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Traceable Chain
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a belief to desire to intention chain.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BDI mental states skill. Build a traceable BDI chain for this agent context: [context]. Include justifications and plan links.

prompt_templates.title: Add Temporal Validity
prompt_templates.scenario: Refine an existing model with time bounds.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BDI mental states skill. Add validity intervals, provenance, and conflict checks to this mental-state model: [model summary].

prompt_templates.title: Validate a BDI Ontology
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a semantic agent design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BDI mental states skill. Review this BDI ontology design for missing grounding, motivation links, justifications, and competency questions: [design].

output_examples.input: A payment reminder arrives for an autonomous finance agent.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a trace from payment reminder world state to belief, desire to avoid late fees, and payment intention.

output_examples.input: A meeting location changes while an assistant agent has an existing plan.
output_examples.output: The skill separates the updated location belief from the meeting time belief and preserves the affected planning chain.

output_examples.input: A team needs queries to test an agent knowledge graph.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests checks for active beliefs, motivating beliefs, fulfilled desires, and ordered plan tasks.

best_practices: Ground every belief in a specific world-state reference.
Attach explicit justifications and validity intervals to mental states.
Keep the ontology small until competency questions require expansion.
anti_patterns: Treating beliefs as raw world facts without a cognitive boundary.
Creating intentions without linked desires, plans, or supporting beliefs.
Expanding ontology classes before validating core competency questions.

faq.question: What does this skill help model?
faq.answer: It helps model beliefs, desires, intentions, plans, justifications, and temporal validity for agents.

faq.question: Does it execute agent actions?
faq.answer: No. It provides modeling guidance and examples for representing agent mental states.

faq.question: Which data formats does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes RDF, Turtle, SPARQL, and ontology patterns for semantic interoperability.

faq.question: When should I use another skill?
faq.answer: Use memory or multi-agent skills when you do not need formal BDI mental-state semantics.

faq.question: Can it support explainability?
faq.answer: Yes. It links beliefs, desires, intentions, plans, and justifications for traceable reasoning.

faq.question: Is it production ready by itself?
faq.answer: No. Treat it as design guidance and validate implementations in your target framework.
